q: Adult systolic still at or above 90, heart rate and breathing up, cool pale clammy skin. What is this?

opts.why: Epinephrine is still holding adult systolic ≥ 90. They can look okay and still be in trouble.
Decompensated shock is when adult systolic falls under 90.
Fast pulse, fast breathing, and cool pale clammy skin are compensated shock, not no shock.
A late crash is decompensated. This stem still has a pressure of 90 or more.

q: Adult systolic falls under 90. Compensatory moves have failed. What is this?

opts.why: Adult systolic under 90 means decompensated (uncompensated on some tests).
Compensated shock still holds adult systolic at or above 90.
A falling systolic with failed compensation is shock, not no shock.
Under 90 means the pressure is no longer holding.

q: What cap-refill cutoff does this recap call delayed in a child?

opts.why: Cap refill over 2 seconds is delayed and matters for shock in kids, even if pressure still looks okay.
The recap’s cutoff is over 2 seconds, not over 4.
The recap’s cutoff is over 2 seconds, not over 5.

q: Trauma, low blood pressure, slow pulse, warm flushed skin below the injury. What type?

opts.why: Cord injury drops sympathetic tone. Almost every other shock speeds the pulse; this one slows it.
Septic is fever and hot skin from infection, not trauma with a slow pulse.
Anaphylaxis is two or more systems after an allergen, not a cord pattern.
Hemorrhagic shock is volume loss. It does not give this slow-pulse cord pattern.

q: Fever or an infection source, hot skin, and low blood pressure. What type?

opts.why: Severe infection dilates and leaks vessels. Hot skin and fever with low pressure is septic.
Neurogenic is trauma, a slow pulse, and a warm line below the injury.
Anaphylaxis needs two or more systems after an allergen, not an infection source.
Hemorrhagic shock is blood loss, not fever and hot skin.

q: After an allergen, how many body systems make this recap call it anaphylaxis?

opts.why: Anaphylaxis is an allergic reaction involving two or more systems (skin, breathing, circulation, gut).
Skin alone is not two or more systems.
Fever is a septic clue. Anaphylaxis is two or more systems after an allergen.
Trauma and a slow pulse is neurogenic, not anaphylaxis.

q: Adult anaphylaxis. What epinephrine dose does this recap want?

opts.why: Adult EpiPen is 0.3 mg IM in the lateral thigh. Hold about 3 seconds. Pediatric is 0.15 mg.
0.15 mg is the pediatric dose, not the adult dose. Same site.
Adult dose in this recap is 0.3 mg, not 0.5 mg. Same site.
Adult dose in this recap is 0.3 mg, not 1.0 mg. Same site.

q: They are in shock. Food and drink?

opts.why: Do not let them eat or drink. It complicates assessment and possible surgery.
Hold drink too. Nothing by mouth.
Hold food too. Nothing by mouth.
Do not delay transport while you try to fix everything on scene.

q: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, possible arrest. ABC or CAB?

opts.why: Suspected cardiac arrest is CAB: circulation and compressions first, then airway and breathing.
ABC is for patients who are still alive. Arrest switches to CAB.
You check breathing and pulse together, then compressions first if there is no pulse.
Start compressions. Use the AED when it arrives; do not wait to start CPR.

q: Unresponsive infant under 1 year. Where do you check a pulse?

opts.why: Infants under 1 year: brachial. Check with breathing, 10 seconds or less.
Carotid is the adult and child site. This stem is an infant: brachial.
This recap’s infant site is brachial, not radial.
This recap’s infant site is brachial, not femoral.

q: How long may you pause compressions in this recap?

q: The AED sees asystole (flatline). What does this recap say it will advise?

opts.why: Shock will not help asystole. The AED says no shock advised. Keep CPR going.
The AED does not restart a flatline. No shock advised.

q: They fainted from a scare, then woke when they were flat. What does this recap want?

opts.why: Psychogenic fainting is not true cellular shock. Still do a full medical eval and check fall injuries.
Do not ignore it because they woke up.
Check injuries from the fall.
This recap says it is not true cells-dying shock.
